samples.summary: Both UI paste paths call `clearCopyBuffer()` unconditionally, so the new "a refused paste leaves the buffer intact" behaviour never holds in the app
samples.evidence: `Worksheet.paste()` at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4899-4901 does `await this.sheet!.paste({ text, html }); this.sheet!.clearCopyBuffer(); this.render();` and `Spreadsheet.paste()` at packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:715-718 does the same. The diff deliberately moved `if (isCut) this.copyBuffer = undefined;` after the merge-split guard (sheet.ts:2290-2295) so a refused paste keeps the cut buffer, and merge.test.ts:209 asserts `isCutMode() === true` after refusal — but through either real entry point the buffer is wiped a line later regardless. The user's cut is silently cancelled (marching ants vanish, nothing moved, no feedback), and a retry falls into the plain-TSV branch, losing formula relocation and merge propagation. The fix belongs in the view callers (only clear when the paste actually happened), or `paste()` must report refusal.

samples.summary: `paste()` gained two silent early-return refusal paths but still returns `void`, so no caller can distinguish refusal from success
samples.evidence: New refusals at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2229-2231 (copied block partially inside source) and 2290-2292 (destination block would be split) return `void`, indistinguishable from a completed paste. Callers packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4899-4901 and packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:715-718 unconditionally clear the buffer, re-render and `notifySelectionChange()`, so the refusal surfaces to the user as a paste that did nothing with no toast/error. `moveRangeTo` has the same void-refusal shape, but drag-move at least leaves the source visibly unmoved; here the clipboard state is destroyed as well (see the companion finding).

samples.summary: `copyBuffer.merges` is a snapshot never invalidated by the other operations that mutate `this.merges`, so a later paste can re-create a block that no longer exists and silently clear destination cells under it
samples.evidence: `copy()`/`cut()` now snapshot `getMergesIntersecting(range)` into `copyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2153, 2173). Nothing invalidates that snapshot: `shiftCells` rewrites the merge map at sheet.ts:1320 (insert/delete rows/cols), `moveRows/moveColumns` at sheet.ts:1509, and `unmergeSelection` deletes blocks at sheet.ts:4540-4542 — none of them touch `copyBuffer` (`clearCopyBuffer` is only called from the views, packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4900/5071 and spreadsheet.ts:716). So: copy a merged range, unmerge it (or insert a row above it), then paste the still-matching clipboard text — `pastedMerges` re-creates the stale block at the destination and `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:927) deletes the destination cells it now covers. Previously the stale buffer could only mis-relocate formulas; it can now delete cell content and create merge geometry that never existed.

samples.summary: Paste is now a merge-mutating path, and `ReadonlyStore.setMerge`/`deleteMerge` are no-ops while `Sheet.merges` is updated anyway, diverging the in-memory map from the store
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:256-262 implements `setMerge`/`deleteMerge` as no-ops, but the new paste code updates the local cache regardless (`this.merges.set(toSref(merge.anchor), merge.span)` at sheet.ts:2342 and `this.merges.delete(...)` at 2338) plus clears cells under the block. `Sheet.paste()` is public and only the view entry points guard read-only (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:690, packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5094), so any other caller on a read-only-store sheet gets a merge map that disagrees with the store until the next `loadMerges()`. Pre-existing for `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4499), but paste widens the exposure.

finding.summary: Both UI paste paths call `clearCopyBuffer()` unconditionally, so the new "a refused paste leaves the buffer intact" behaviour never holds in the app

verdict.reason: Verified in the working tree. sheet.ts:2290-2295 refuses a merge-splitting paste with a bare `return` and deliberately clears the cut buffer only afterwards ("so a refused paste leaves the buffer intact"), and merge.test.ts:209 asserts isCutMode() stays true after refusal. But `paste()` returns void with no refusal signal, and both UI entry points call clearCopyBuffer() unconditionally on the very next line: worksheet.ts:4899-4901 (reached from the Ctrl+V keybinding in the same keymap block as Escape/copy/cut at 5066-5090) and spreadsheet.ts:715-718 (public method). clearCopyBuffer() (sheet.ts:2133-2135) sets copyBuffer = undefined, so through either real path the invariant never holds: isCutMode() — consumed by the overlay at worksheet.ts:5554 — goes false, and a retry no longer matches `text === this.copyBuffer.text` (sheet.ts:2209), falling into the plain-TSV branch at 2253-2256 and losing formula relocation and merge propagation. No guard elsewhere prevents this; the only other clearCopyBuffer() call (worksheet.ts:5070) is the explicit Escape cancel. This is in-lane for blast radius: an invariant established in the changed model is defeated by unchanged callers in files the diff does not show, and it is a caller-left-inconsistent/violated-invariant defect at major severity.

verdict.reason: The two new refusals do exist (sheet.ts:2229-2231, 2290-2292), but paste() already had silent void refusal paths on the identical contract before this change — sheet.ts:2189 (pivot), 2257-2259 (no clipboard payload), 2265-2266 (no pasteRange) — with a test locking that shape in (pivot-protection.test.ts:52-60). The interface a caller sees is unchanged: still Promise<void>, same nullability/async/throw set. Every caller (view/worksheet.ts:4899-4901, view/spreadsheet.ts:715-718 whose own public paste already returns silently at :690, frontend sheet-view.tsx:757-759) was already written for a paste that may legitimately no-op, and none passes rejected arguments, relies on a removed export, or branches on a changed result. Silent refusal is also the repo-wide pattern: moveRangeTo (sheet.ts:2445/2475/2482) is void, and autofill's boolean is used only to pick render vs renderOverlay (worksheet.ts:4165-4171), with no user feedback either. So no caller is left broken and no guard is bypassed; the ask is new result-type + notification plumbing, i.e. a design-fit/UX concern statable without leaving the diff — out of this lens's lane. The genuinely blast-radius part of the cited evidence (callers clearing the copy buffer despite sheet.ts:2293-2295 preserving it on refusal) is the reviewer's separate companion finding and is unaffected by this refutation.

finding.evidence: `copy()`/`cut()` now snapshot `getMergesIntersecting(range)` into `copyBuffer` (sheet.ts:2153, 2173). Nothing invalidates that snapshot: `shiftCells` rewrites the merge map at sheet.ts:1320 (insert/delete rows/cols), `moveRows/moveColumns` at sheet.ts:1509, and `unmergeSelection` deletes blocks at sheet.ts:4540-4542 — none of them touch `copyBuffer` (`clearCopyBuffer` is only called from the views, packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4900/5071 and spreadsheet.ts:716). verdict.reason: Verified independently: `copyBuffer` is private to sheet.ts and every one of its 13 references is a declaration, a copy/cut write, a reader, or the cut-clear — none in any mutation path. Repo-wide (case-insensitive) search finds only three `clearCopyBuffer()` callers, all in views (after paste, and on Escape), so no structural operation invalidates the snapshot. `shiftCells` wholesale-replaces the merge map (sheet.ts:1320) and `unmergeSelection` deletes blocks (sheet.ts:4539-4543) without touching the buffer; since unmerge does not change cell content, the clipboard text still matches and the internal-paste branch (sheet.ts:2209) still fires. Paste re-validates the snapshot only geometrically (sheet.ts:2229 isRangeInRange against sourceRange, and the destination overlap check at 2285-2292) — there is no check that the copied anchors still exist in `this.merges`. `pastedMerges` is rebuilt from the stale snapshot (2232-2235) and applied at 2340-2348, where `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:927-965) deletes destination cells under the re-created block, and paste passes no `keep` predicate (contrast moveRangeTo at sheet.ts:2567). No test covers the stale ordering: merge.test.ts:213-229 unmerges only after pasting. Reachable copy -> unmerge -> paste therefore recreates merge geometry that no longer exists and clears destination content: a violated invariant in undiffed code, in-lane for blast radius, major.
